A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ectomycorrhiza are more efficient to provide host plants with P in the presence of high soil P availability than in the presence of low soil P availability.

, in a P-limited soil, the fungus is able to colonize the soil at a high rate and to transfer a large quantity of P to the host plant, whereas in a soil with high P availability, fungal colonization is slower but the fungus is still able to transfer a large amount of P to the plant.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ectomycrorhizal symbiosis is more efficient to improve P nutrition of host plant in high soil P conditions.
ectomycorrhiza can be an important P transfer mechanism in soils with low P availability, but can also contribute to plant P nutrition in soils with high P availability, despite its lower efficiency.
, despite the fact that the ectomycorhizal symbiosis is less efficient in colonizing the soil when P is high, the fungus still provides more P to the host plant than it takes up from the soil.
